stem: How would you determine the standard electrode potential of the system \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\,|\,\text{Mg}\)?
Can you store copper sulphate solutions in a zinc pot?
Consult the table of standard electrode potentials and suggest three substances that can oxidise ferrous ions under suitable conditions.

Represent the cell in which the following reaction takes place
\(\text{Mg}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^{+}(0.0001\,\text{M}) \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+}(0.130\,\text{M}) + 2\text{Ag}(s)\)
Calculate its \(E_{(cell)}\) if \(E^{\circ}_{(cell)} = 3.17\,\text{V}\).
_note: In the printed first line of the solution the concentration terms are set WITHOUT square brackets (a bare \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\) over \(\text{Ag}^{+2}\)); the surrounding text and every other Nernst expression in this chapter use \([\;]\). Transcribed with the brackets restored — typesetting only, the quantity is unchanged.

stem:
Calculate the equilibrium constant of the reaction:
\(\text{Cu}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^{+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Ag}(s)\)
\(E^{\circ}_{(cell)} = 0.46\,\text{V}\)

The standard electrode potential for Daniell cell is \(1.1\,\text{V}\). Calculate the standard Gibbs energy for the reaction:
\(\text{Zn}(s) + \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cu}(s)\)
solution:
\(\Delta_r G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{(cell)}\)

\(n\) in the above equation is 2, \(F = 96487\,\text{C mol}^{-1}\) and \(E^{\circ}_{(cell)} = 1.1\,\text{V}\)

Therefore, \(\Delta_r G^{\circ} = -2 \times 1.1\,\text{V} \times 96487\,\text{C mol}^{-1}\)

\(= -21227\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\)

\(= -212.27\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)
_note: PRINTED DEFECT, transcribed faithfully: the intermediate line reads \(-21227\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\), which has lost a digit. \(2 \times 1.1 \times 96487 = 212271.4\), so the line should read \(-212271\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\). The book's own FINAL answer \(-212.27\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\) is correct and follows from the corrected intermediate, not from the printed one (which would give \(-21.227\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\)), so the defect is confined to that one line.
